newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends mostly down on correction.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends mostly down on correction.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mostly down in dull trading on Wednesday on a technical correction after sharp gains on Tuesday, traders said.
The most active May 1997 contract ended at 21,760 yuan ($2,623) per tonne, losing 120 yuan. It opened at an intra-day low of 21,650 and hit a high of 21,820.
February rose 10 to 21,430, March fell 30 to 21,500, April was down 100 at 21,680 and June 110 to 21,770. July rose 350 to 21,950.
Combined volume fell to 25,820 tonnes from 70,620.

Copper opened sharply lower on profit-taking triggered by overnight losses on the London Metal Exchange (LME), but speculative buying at low levels pushed prices from their lows, traders said. Copper would consolidate at the current level in the short term, they said.
"Retail investors dominated today's trade, pushing the prices up and down, but copper is unlikely to fluctuate sharply given a lack of market-moving news," one trader said.
"Firm spot copper prices prevented copper futures from falling further despite today's profit-taking," he added.

The spot copper price remained above 21,200 yuan per tonne in Shanghai. Traders said investors would not build large fresh positions with the approach of the Chinese lunar new year holiday, which begins on February 6.
"Copper will follow the LME over the next few days given the absence of domestic interest in trading," a second trader said.

Aluminium ended sharply up on LME gains. February rose 160 to 15,360 yuan per tonne, March 290 to 15,690, April 150 to 15,900 and May 450 to 16,050. Combined volume fell to 1,820 tonnes from 3,040. ($1=8.2956 yuan)
